primary_artifact: /Volumes/HMI-Library/heavy-metal-index-raw/reports/Commission Regulation (EU) 2023-915 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food.pdf
disposition_reason: Annex I entry 3.2.15 sets cadmium maximum levels for four cocoa and chocolate product classes (milk chocolate <30% total dry cocoa solids 0,10; chocolate <50% / milk chocolate >=30% 0,30; chocolate >=50% 0,80; consumer cocoa powder incl. drinking-chocolate ingredient 0,60 mg/kg). No lead, mercury, arsenic or nickel ML names cocoa or chocolate in this original 2023 text.
disposition_locator: Annex I, section 3.2 Cadmium, entries 3.2.15.1-3.2.15.4 and footnote (14); PDF p. 35 (OJ L 119/137 approx.); Article 11 entry into force

unresolved: The original 2023/915 text read here predates the nickel amendment (EU) 2024/1987; nickel MLs for chocolate/cocoa powder are recorded under eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels.
Out-of-scope analytes noted but not recorded: ochratoxin A 3,0 µg/kg in cocoa powder (entry 1.2.16) and PAH limits for cocoa beans/derived products incl. cocoa butter (5.1.4) and cocoa fibre (5.1.5).
Generic tin (inorganic) ML 200 mg/kg for canned food (3.5.1) would cover canned cocoa products but names no cocoa product; not recorded as a cocoa limit.
No EU maximum level applies to raw cocoa beans or nibs for cadmium; Article 3 (dried/processed/compound food factors) governs foods not listed.
